item.title: Falconer's conjecture through descent and chaining
item.description: arXiv:2611.14867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI proved that a compact set $E\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d}{2}$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive length. We give a complete proof of this theorem which follows the overall architecture of the OpenAI argument, from the construction of the initial pair measures to the final Fourier estimate, but which modifies that argument substantially at the points where the geometric costs are paid and where the estimates are reassembled. The reductions are organized by the descent and chaining viewpoint of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause: one potential, built from two separated depths together with a penalty for insufficient separation, pays for every reduction on every interval of scales, the terminal intervals included, and a finite-record chaining lemma keeps the fixed power losses attached to the few reductions which incur them. In odd dimensions the radial improvement is obtained directly at each finite scale from a quantitative contact interval, chosen by minimizing a mass curve against lines of two slopes, with explicit margins in place of a compactness argument, and the conditional estimates on the three parts of that interval are multiplied by a lemma on full source fibers. A random sign identity represents the coarse pair filter by products of endpoint multipliers and reduces the cost of reassembling the spatial pieces inside the shell estimate. The argument gives more than positive length. Since the mass first excluded near heavy hyperplanes at each late scale is summable with a power rate, all the Fourier estimates compare with one fixed measure, and the distance set supports a probability measure with an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$ and with power Fourier decay, so that $\Delta(E)$ has positive Fourier dimension.
item.dc:creator: Will Burstein, Alex Iosevich, Alexia Yavicoli

item.title: Sharp weighted bounds for reverse fractional integral operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.15075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the one-weight reverse fractional integral operators \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^q(w^q)}\geq C_w\|f\|_{L^p(w^p)} \] holds for all nonnegative measurable functions $f$, with $\frac ns<p<1$ and $\frac1q=\frac1p-\frac sn$, if and only if $w^{p/(1-p)}\in A_{\frac{p(s-n)}{n(1-p)}}$. Furthermore, we show the lower bound \[ C_w\gtrsim_{n,s,p}[w]_{p,q}^{\min\left\{\frac{p(n-s)}{n(1-p)},\frac{p(n-s)}{sp-n}\right\}}, \] and the exponent is sharp. We also investigate when the reverse weak-type estimate \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}(w^{\frac{n}{n-s}})}\geq \frac{n}{s}\,v_n^{(n-s)/n}[w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}]^{(n-s)/n}_{A_1}\|f\|_{L^1(w)} \] holds if and only if $w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}\in A_1$.
item.dc:creator: Liang Huang, Hanli Tang

item.title: Sharp L^p and variation inequalities for maximal operators on finite connected graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.15377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=(V_G,E_G)$ be a finite connected graph (here $V_G$ and $E_G$ denote the set of vertices and edges of $G$ respectively). The primary aim of this paper is to study the sharp variation and $L^p$ inequalities of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator $M_G$ defined on $G$ and its fractional variant $M_{\alpha,G}\,(0<\alpha<1)$). Set $${\bf C}_{\alpha,G}^{p,q}=\sup\limits_{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)>0}\frac{{\rm Var}_{q,G}(M_{\alpha,G}f)}{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)},$$ where ${\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)$ denotes the $p$-variation of $f$ on $G$. We denote by $K_n$ (resp., $S^n$) the complete (resp., star) graph with $n\geq4$ vertices. When $\alpha=0$, we prove ${\bf C}_{\alpha,S_n}^{p,p} =1-\frac{1}{n}$ for $0<p<1$. This solve a question originally posed by Liu and Xue in 2021. In the fractional case $0<\alpha<1$, we prove ${\bf C}_{\alpha,S_n}^{1,q}=1-n^{-\alpha}$ and ${\bf C}_{\alpha,K_n}^{1,q} =(1-n^{\alpha-1})(n-1)^{-\alpha}$ for $q=\frac{1}{1-\alpha}$, which provide some examples focusing on sharp variation inequalities of fractional maximal operators. The sharp variation inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operators are also established. In addition, the sharp $L^p$ inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operator $\widetilde{M}_{\alpha,G}$ are also studied. More precisely, we obtain lower bounds and upper bounds for $C_{q,G}$ such that the inequality $\|\widetilde{M}_{\alpha,G}f\|_q\leq C_{q,G}\|f\|_p$ holds and the complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$ are two extreme graphs that reach the lower bound and upper bound respectively.
item.dc:creator: Feng Liu, Yongzhi Lian, Yanzhen Wang

item.title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
item.description: arXiv:2611.15402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\Theta\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $\Theta(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\in\Theta$. We prove that $\Theta(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_H\Theta>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. The same framework can be used to show that if $\tau$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the similarity group with finite $\bigl(\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1\bigr)$-energy, then every compactly supported $\tau$-stationary probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ has a smooth density. We deduce that a nonempty compact set has nonempty interior if its family of similarity self-embeddings has Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1$.
item.dc:creator: Daewoong Cheong, Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen

item.title: Directional maximal functions along algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.15517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the maximal operator over line segments in $N$ arbitrary directions on a real algebraic curve of degree $D$ in $\mathbb R^n$ has $L^2$ operator norm at most $C_{n,\varepsilon}D^{C_n}N^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, with $C_n$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Combined with polynomial partitioning, this gives the sharp bound $N^{\frac14}$, up to a polylogarithmic factor, for $N$ arbitrary directions in $\mathbb R^3$. The first main ingredient is a new quantitative strengthening of the property that the curve crosses each affine hyperplane at most $D$ times. This condition controls the overlap of variable-width neighborhoods of hyperplanes. The width attached to each direction is a small multiple of its distance to the osculating hyperplane at an endpoint of its arc. The problem is projectively invariant, and a projective almost orthogonality principle turns the overlap control into the $L^2$ bound. The second main ingredient, building on the complex cellular preparation of Binyamini and Novikov, is a new effective decomposition of algebraic curves. Up to $D^{C_n}$ points, the curve is covered by $D^{C_n}$ arcs whose coordinates, in a suitable parametrization and projective frame, are monomials with distinct exponents times nearly constant units. In these charts we verify the quantitative crossing condition with polynomial dependence on $D$. The framework also applies to nonalgebraic curves with doubling Frenet curvature measures. Consequences include local Sobolev maximal estimates along measurable vector fields with values in an algebraic curve, and the same bounds, up to a logarithmic factor, for directional Calder\'on--Zygmund operators.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Di Plinio, Ioannis Parissis

item.title: Artin-style characterizations of the multiple gamma and sine functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Artin's characterizations of the gamma function to the multiple setting by means of the Kubert identity. We obtain uniqueness theorems for positive continuous solutions of a difference equation $G(z + 1) = \alpha(z)G(z)$ that also satisfy an Artin-type multiplication formula, remaining within the class of continuous functions under a modest initial condition. The results apply in particular to the Barnes multiple gamma functions and the Kurokawa multiple sine functions.
item.dc:creator: Genki Shibukawa

item.title: Exceptional parameters in the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.15734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Erd\H os similarity conjecture says that for every infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, there exists a set $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure which does not contain any affine copy of $x + tA$ of $A$ (with $t \neq 0$). Kolountzakis proved that for every infinite $A$, there exists $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure so that the exceptional sets $D_E(A)$ of scales $t$, and $\mathcal E_E(A)$ of affine maps $(x,t)$, for which $x+tA\subseteq E$, are both Lebesgue null. We show that these exceptional parameter sets are small in two finer senses. First, given any countable family of Fourier decay rates, a single $E$ can be constructed so that $D_E(A)$ is null with respect to every measure whose Fourier transform decays at one of these rates. Consequently, there are compact sets $K$ of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ for which $D_K(A)$ and $\mathcal E_K(A)$ have modified Fourier dimension zero. Second, we give a criterion, depending both on the growth of a gauge function $h$ and on the gaps between elements of lacunary sequences in $A$, which guarantees that $\mathcal H^h(D_E(A))=0$ for gauges with $h(u)/u\to\infty$, as well as a similar result for $\mathcal E_K(A)$. For sets such as $A = \{1/n!\}$ and $A = \{e^{-n^q}\}$, this yields explicit gauges of the form $h(u) = u\exp((\log 1/u)^\theta)$ with $0 < \theta < 1$.
item.dc:creator: Neeraja Kulkarni, Natalia Mora Cu\'ellar

item.title: A short route to Diening's averaging criterion in spaces of homogeneous type
item.description: arXiv:2611.15808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a short, self-contained proof of the averaging-operator criterion for the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over unbounded spaces of homogeneous type. Building on techniques of Diening and Lerner, we establish a Jensen-type inequality with uniformly summable error, from which the criterion follows directly via a Calder\'on-Zygmund argument.
item.dc:creator: Alina Shalukhina

item.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.15970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Deodhar

item.title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
item.description: arXiv:2611.15972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.
item.dc:creator: Nino Anakidze, M\'at\'e Szilveszter, George Tephnadze, Ferenc Weisz

item.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.16007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(\sigma)$ to $L^q(\omega)$ for the operator $H_\sigma g(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,d\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $\omega$ is a $\sigma$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $\kappa_{p,q}$ in $C_*\le\kappa_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $\omega$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Os\k{e}kowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Kanjilal

item.title: Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length
item.description: arXiv:2611.16547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. After translating the variable, every such sequence is a finite rational Darboux transform of an explicit family with differential order $m$ and eigenvalue $n$. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the factors determine all polynomial differential eigenoperators of the resulting family. For families that cannot be obtained by these transformations from families of smaller minimum differential order, the minimum differential and recurrence orders coincide. All such families are classified in minimum differential orders at least three, including additional families in composite orders.
item.dc:creator: K. Castillo

item.title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
item.description: arXiv:2611.16580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Buchecker, Benjamin Eichinger

item.title: On the size of the defect set of an analytic matrix field
item.description: arXiv:2611.16660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we study the defect set of a symmetric analytic matrix field $M$ defined on an open set $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge2$. A defect point $x \in \Omega$ of $M$ is defined as a point for which no eigenframe can be chosen continuously in any neighborhood of $x$. We show that the defect set $S(M)$ is contained in a locally finite union of analytic submanifolds of codimension at least $2$. The proof follows fairly directly from results by Parusinski and Rond (Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 2020) and by Kurdyka and Paunescu (Duke Math. J., 2008). This result can be applied in the context of the Landau-de Gennes Theory to estimate the physical defects of a nematic liquid crystal.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Aubertin

item.title: On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.16945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.
item.dc:creator: Ignasi Guill\'en-Mola

item.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.17002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.
item.dc:creator: Yingyu Zhao, Yunhao Zhao

item.title: On transformations in the Second Painlev\'e family
item.description: arXiv:2611.17179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We complete the classification of algebraic relations among solutions of equations in the second Painlev\'e family $P_{II}(\alpha): y''=2y^3+ty+\alpha$, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$. More precisely, we prove that if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generic solutions of $P_{II}(\alpha_1),\ldots,P_{II}(\alpha_n)$, respectively, and $tr.deg_{\mathbb{C}(t)}\mathbb{C}(t)(y_1,y_1',\ldots,y_n,y_n')<2n$, then for some $i<j$, we have that $\alpha_i\pm\alpha_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $y_i=T(y_j)$ for a classical B\"acklund transformation $T$. In particular, the classical B\"acklund transformations are the only B\"acklund transformations in the second Painlev\'e family.
item.dc:creator: Christine Eagles, Joel Nagloo

item.title: Patterns, Distances, and Structure in Sparse Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.17198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central theme in modern harmonic analysis, with strong connections to Ramsey theory, is the tension between randomness and structure: to what extent can a "large" set avoid prescribed configurations, and when must such patterns inevitably appear? The answer depends delicately on how size is measured, with notions such as Hausdorff dimension, Fourier dimension, and density leading to strikingly different phenomena. In this mini-course, we explore this theme through two complementary perspectives. On one hand, we study translation-invariant linear patterns, a natural class of Euclidean Ramsey-type configurations. On the other hand, we investigate distance sets of sparse subsets of Euclidean space, which encode metric configurations of pairs of points. Together, these results illustrate a unifying principle: while sparse sets may avoid individual configurations, sufficiently strong analytic or geometric conditions enforce the emergence of Ramsey-type structure. The course will emphasize key ideas, methods, and examples, aiming to provide an accessible entry point to current developments at the interface of harmonic analysis, geometric measure theory, and Euclidean Ramsey theory. Lectures are by Malabika Pramanik.
item.dc:creator: Paige Bright

item.title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.14807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Juan Jos\'e Mar\'in

item.title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
item.description: arXiv:2611.15505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately. Starting from $33592$ formal interlacing words, published necessary restrictions leave $13404$ candidates. Integer realization certificates and $53$ exact exclusion stages classify every candidate. The surviving set agrees exactly with the set of certified realizations. All verification uses integer and rational arithmetic. The accompanying code, certificates, proof notes, and per-word exclusion ledger make the computation reproducible. The result concerns degree six; it does not resolve the classification problem in arbitrary degree or count connected components of coefficient space. Most of the mathematical development, code, certificates, and initial manuscript were generated using ChatGPT under the author's direction. No independent human audit of the complete proof chain has yet been completed.
item.dc:creator: Andrej A. Novikov

item.title: How to arrange four points in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.16990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[ D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[ \begin{cases} \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1, \text{a rhombus with angle }\theta\in(\pi/3,\pi/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1. \end{cases} \]
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.
item.dc:creator: Danqing He, Xuancheng Shao

item.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Kittle, Constantin Kogler

item.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.17293v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.
item.dc:creator: Ciprian Demeter, William O'Regan

item.title: Rational limit cycles of Abel differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2302.10743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the number of rational limit cycles of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A(t)$ and $B(t)$ are real trigonometric polynomials. We show that this number is at most the degree of $A(t)$ plus one.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Electron. J. Qual. Theory Differ. Equ. 2023, No. 47, 1-13
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Luis Bravo, Luis \'Angel Calder\'on, Ignacio Ojeda

item.title: Stability of singular limit cycles for Abel equations revisited
item.description: arXiv:2302.13642v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A criterion is obtained for the semi-stability of the isolated singular positive closed solutions, i.e., singular positive limit cycles, of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A,B$ are smooth functions with two zeros in the interval $[0,T]$ and where these singular positive limit cycles satisfy certain conditions, which allows an upper bound on the number of limit cycles of the Abel equation to be obtained. The criterion is illustrated by obtaining an upper bound of two positive limit cycles for the family $A(t)=t(t-t_A)$, $B(t)=(t-t_B)(t-1)$, $t\in[0,1]$. In the linear trigonometric case, i.e., when $A(t)=a_0+a_1\sin t +a_2\cos t$, $B(t)=b_0+b_1\sin t+b_2\cos t$, an upper bound of two limit cycles is also obtained for $a_0,b_0$ sufficiently small and in the region where two positive limit cycles bifurcate from the origin.
item.dc:creator: J. L. Bravo, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda

item.title: Mehler Formula for Wronskians of Hermite Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2606.02405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the bilinear generating function for Wronskians of Hermite polynomials can be expressed as the classical Mehler kernel multiplied by a polynomial, thereby extending the result of Pupasov-Maksimov [Ann. Physics 363 (2015), 122-135, arXiv:1502.01778] for exceptional Hermite polynomials. We establish several properties of the polynomials appearing in this extended version of the Mehler formula and present four conjectures about them.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kuznetsov, Minjian Yuan

item.title: The general Brannan coefficient conjecture II: Meijer-function approximations
item.description: arXiv:2606.11621v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The coefficients $A_n(\alpha,\beta,\omega)$ in the Maclaurin expansion $(1+\omega z)^{\alpha}(1-z)^{-\beta}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} A_n(\alpha,\beta,\omega)z^n$ are considered for $|\omega|=1$ and $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]$. D. A. Brannan conjectured in a 1973 paper that $|A_n(\alpha,\beta,\omega)|\le A_n(\alpha,\beta,1)$ for every positive odd integer $n$. The present author recently established the conjecture outside a small neighbourhood of $\omega=-1$. The remaining range is treated here by combining compound Laplace integral representations with two types of local approximation: a Meijer $G$ function approximation for $n|\arg(-\omega)|$ bounded, and a modified Watson approximation for the complementary range. The resulting lower bounds reduce the problem to numerical positivity checks for explicit functions on compact parameter sets. These computations verify the inequality for all $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]$ and all odd integers $n\ge5$, and hence, together with Brannan's result for $n=3$, complete the proof of his conjecture.
item.dc:creator: T. M. Dunster

item.title: Orthonormal bases of spherical harmonics with maximal Lp norm growth
item.description: arXiv:2609.14023v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show that for every p>2, there is an orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics on the n-dimensional unit sphere which achieves the maximal Lp norm growth. More precisely, one basis achieves this growth for p up to the critical exponent 2(n+1)/(n-1), and another for p from the critical exponent up to infinity. The first basis is built from rotations of the real part of a highest weight spherical harmonic. The second is built from zonal harmonics whose poles are selected from a spherical design. In both cases, the selection uses the restricted invertibility theorem of Bourgain and Tzafriri. This extends earlier results of Bourgain and of the author (arXiv:1404.5016) on the 2-dimensional sphere for 2<p<=6 to all dimensions and all p>2, and improves the positive density subsequence there to a whole basis.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: Wave Packet Density in Local Smoothing: Refinements and Limitations
item.description: arXiv:2609.34675v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a transverse covering $L^2$ argument that both substantially simplifies the approach of Gan, He, Li, and Wu and improves their local smoothing estimates for Fourier integral operators with positive conic curvature in even spatial dimensions $n\geq 4$. We also investigate the limitations of wave packet density methods, showing that genuine geometric obstructions already arise in the Euclidean setting.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Pitt Inequalities and Logarithmic-type Uncertainty Principles for Metaplectic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2609.34946v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we provide a complete characterisation of Pitt's inequality for metaplectic operators. The symplectic geometry underlying a metaplectic operator distinguishes effective directions, along which its action is Fourier-type, from singular directions, along which concentration is preserved. For this reason, we adopt two complementary perspectives, thereby obtaining both an isotropic Pitt's inequality, emulating the classical theorem of Pitt, and an anisotropic inequality that adapts to the geometric features of the metaplectic group. As a by-product, we obtain Pitt's inequality for Fourier transforms along subspaces of $\rd$ and new quantitative time-dependent boundedness results for metaplectic operators on homogeneous Sobolev spaces, with applications to Schr\"odinger evolutions generated by quadratic Hamiltonians. Additionally, we derive logarithmic and entropic uncertainty principles for the metaplectic group. We show that the classical entropic uncertainty principle fails when both the effective and singular directions are present. In this case, a generally unbounded corrective entropy term accounts for the concentration-preserving directions and restores a meaningful lower bound. For quadratic Schr\"odinger evolutions, this correction follows the time-dependent geometry of the nondispersive directions and adjusts the uncertainty estimate accordingly.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Giacchi, Itamar Oliveira, Amy Tierney

item.title: Gamma-Convergence of Weak-Type Nonlocal Functionals
item.description: arXiv:2610.07001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$ be a bounded open interval when $N=1$ or a bounded Lipschitz domain when $N\ge2$. For $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, consider the weak-type nonlocal functional \begin{align*} F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(u;\Omega):=\lambda^p \underset{\scriptscriptstyle |u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}} {\int_\Omega\int_\Omega}|x-y|^{\gamma-N}\,dy\,dx \end{align*} with $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ measurable. We prove that, as $\lambda\to\infty$ for $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$ or as $\lambda\to0^+$ for $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, $F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(\cdot;\Omega)$ converges, in the sense of $\Gamma$-convergence in $L^p(\Omega)$, to \begin{align*} \Psi_{p,\gamma}^{\Omega}(u) :=\begin{cases} C_{N,p,\gamma}^{\rm cell}\displaystyle\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^p\,dx, &p\in(1,\infty)\ \hbox{and}\ u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega),\\ C_{N,1,\gamma}^{\rm cell}|Du|(\Omega), &p=1\ \hbox{and}\ u\in BV(\Omega),\\ \infty,&\hbox{otherwise}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the positive constants $C_{N,p,\gamma}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ are independent of $\Omega$. We also establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of $F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(\cdot;\mathbb R^N)$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^N)$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with the limit functional having an additional term when $(N,p,\gamma)=(1,1,-1)$. These results affirmatively answer [Open Problem~9.3, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 2023] of Brezis and also the other problem by Brezis et al. in [Section~7C, Anal. PDE 2024].
item.dc:creator: Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang

item.title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function
item.description: arXiv:2610.40100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$ \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x) =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,d\sigma(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, when the supremum is restricted to a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii, the norm of the resulting operator from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ grows at least like $\log N$. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$.
item.dc:creator: Sanghyuk Lee, Ji Li, Chaojie Wen, Liangchuan Wu

item.title: Resolving Tusn\'ady's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06998v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a lower bound of $\Omega_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusn\'ady's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors. The matching upper and lower bounds are also formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2112.14662v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $\rho(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarn\'ik-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Sodin

item.title: Combinatorics of generalized orthogonal polynomials of type $R_{II}$
item.description: arXiv:2411.12345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1995, Ismail and Masson introduced orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \), which are defined by specific three-term recurrence relations with additional conditions. Recently, Kim and Stanton found a combinatorial interpretation for the moments of orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_I \) in the spirit of the combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials due to Flajolet and Viennot. In this paper, we push this combinatorial model further to orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \). Moreover, we generalize orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \) by relaxing some of their conditions. We then prove a master theorem, which generalizes combinatorial models for moments of various types of orthogonal polynomials: classical orthogonal polynomials, Laurent biorthogonal polynomials, and orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \).
item.dc:creator: Jang Soo Kim, Minho Song

item.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
item.description: arXiv:2508.05573v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $\epsilon$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results. We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ars Inveniendi Analytica (2026), Paper No. 6, 49 pp
item.dc:creator: Pierre Germain, Simon L. Rydin Myerson, Daniel Pezzi

item.title: Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
item.description: arXiv:2605.14699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragi\v{c}evi\'c for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schr\"odinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio

item.title: Improvement of a Hardy-Littlewood inequality and applications to the boundedness of analytic paraproducts on mixed norm spaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.28080v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ denote the space of analytic functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For $0<p<\infty$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, let $M_p^p(r,f)=\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^p \frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$ and $M_\infty(r,f) = \sup_{|z|=r}|f(z)|$. For $0<p<q\leq \infty$, Hardy and Littlewood proved the prevalent inequality $$M_q(r,f)\le C(p,q)\frac{M_p(\rho,f)}{(\rho-r)^{\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}}}$$ for $0\leq r<\rho\leq 1$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$. In this paper, we obtain an improvement of this well-known inequality which is employed to characterize the symbols $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ such that the analytic paraproducts $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(\zeta)g'(\zeta)\,d\zeta$, $S_gf(z)=\int_0^z f'(\zeta)g(\zeta)\,d\zeta$ and $M_gf(z)=f(z)g(z)$, are bounded between two different mixed-norm spaces $A^{p,q}_\omega=\{ g\in \mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}): \int_0^1 M_p^q(r,g) \omega(r)\,dr<\infty\}$ induced by a radial doubling weight $\omega$. En route to the proof of these characterizations, we consider an open Carleson measure problem posed by Luecking and we solve it in a meaningful particular case.
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Miguel Moreno, Jos\'e \'Angel Pel\'aez

item.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{\xi\in \mathbb F_q^d:\xi_1^2+\cdots+\xi_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, d\sigma)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $\eta_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $\eta_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34758v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. Let $M_{GP,d}(p)$ be the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression. For every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, we prove \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Dung The Tran, Boqing Xue

item.title: On Fourier frames
item.description: arXiv:math/0005092v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We solve the problem of Duffin and Schaeffer (1952) of characterizing those sequences of real frequencies which generate Fourier frames. Equivalently, we characterize the sampling sequences for the Paley-Wiener space. The key step is to connect the problem with de Branges' theory of Hilbert spaces of entire functions. We show that our description of sampling sequences permits us to obtain a classical inequality of H. Landau as a consequence of Pavlov's description of Riesz bases of complex exponentials and the John-Nirenberg theorem. Finally, we discuss how to transform our description into a working condition by relating it to an approximation problem for subharmonic functions. By this approach, we determine the critical growth rate of a nondecreasing function $\psi$ such that the sequence $\{\lamdda_k\}){k\in \Bbb Z}$ defined by $\lambda_k + \psi(\lambda_k)=k$ is a sampling.
item.dc:creator: Joaquim Ortega-Cerda, Kristian Seip
